ideas.title: Merge Up: Will 1,024 Rocks Become the Sun?
ideas.hook: A glowing glass jar with grey rocks already dropping in and pairs merging into bigger, brighter balls; yellow 'BIGGEST: 8' counter ticking up
ideas.why: LED Physics' 'Will 1,024 rocks become the Sun? #shorts' is at 1,031,751 views (99.3x its channel average, 6 days old), the biggest Short outlier in today's trending pull. It is a count-up-to-a-big-number payoff like your string art and brick breaker Shorts (89-107% watched), and the review says to keep Shorts at 20-30 s with a visible finish line. It uses only the existing physics (circles + collision), so it is a Test slot, not an upgrade.
ideas.format: Bounce Theory · Merge Up (new sims.py function merge_up)
ideas.script:
Build: new merge_up() in sims.py. 1080x1920, 60 fps, near-black background, saturated glowing colours. A tall glass jar outline (white, 4 px glow) at x 190-890, y 480-1380. Balls drop one at a time from the top every 0.5 s at a pre-seeded x position. Tier ladder (each tier doubles): 1 Rock (grey), 2 Stone (brown), 4 Ember (red-orange), 8 Coal-glow (orange), 16 Lava (amber), 32 Fireball (yellow), 64 Star-dust (white-yellow), 128 Comet (cyan), 256 Planet (magenta), 512 Giant (violet), 1,024 SUN (gold with rotating rays). Radius grows 1.3x per tier (start 18 px). Rule: when two balls of the same tier touch they merge into the next tier at the contact point with a small spark ring; real gravity and bounce, the seed is rigged so the final merge happens at 24-26 s. On-screen lines (white + yellow, y 120-1450): white 'WILL 1,024 ROCKS BECOME THE SUN?' at y=180; yellow 'BIGGEST: 8' counter at y=290 updating on each new top tier; small white tier name above each new ball for 1 s. Win condition: two 512 Giants merge into the Sun, white flash 0.3 s, Sun fills the jar with rotating rays, yellow 'THE SUN' for 2 s. Looping ending: the Sun shrinks back to a grey rock and the first rock drops again. Sound (all synthesized): soft plink on drop, rising pentatonic note per merge (pitch by tier), low whoosh + chord swell on the Sun. Length 26-30 s.
Description: 1,024 rocks, one jar. Does it become the Sun? Watch to the end.

ideas.script:
New sims.py function spiral_chain(). Arena: Archimedean spiral wall (r = 60 + 34·θ, 4.5 turns, line width 6) centred at (540, 900), rotating 0.35 rad/s; a glowing core circle r=45 at the centre. Start with 1 ball (r=14). Rule: every time a ball hits the spiral wall it splits into 2 (child gets ±15° velocity jitter), capped at 999 balls; ball radius shrinks from 14 to 6 as count grows. Gravity off; balls get a constant inward pull of 60 px/s² so they creep toward the core. Each ball's hue = its generation (rainbow cycle). Counter top-centre counts up. Win: first ball that touches the core triggers the core to flash and absorb all balls in a 2 s vacuum swirl. Looping ending: after the swirl, one white ball pops out of the core and flies back to the spiral mouth (= frame 1). On-screen lines (y=140-320): white 'Every hit = 2 balls', yellow 'Can 1 reach the centre? 🌀'; counter '1 → 999' at y≈1420. Sound: each split plays the next note of 'Ode to Joy' (public domain, synthesized bell timbre, max 12 notes/sec, gain rises with count); core hit = deep boom + whoosh. Background #06060b, spiral glow electric blue #3a7bff.
